title: IMPERATOR: The Burden of the Danube

raetian_frontier.name: Alpine Pressure
raetian_frontier.text: After this Army Musters to Strength 4 or more, lose 1 Supply.

marcomannia.name: Deep Incursion
marcomannia.text: When this Army devastates a Roman base, lose 1 additional Rome.

quadi.name: Fractured Kingship
quadi.text: Whenever this Army Musters, increase Coalition by 1.

iazyges.name: Sarmatian Horsemen
iazyges.text: In a Clash, the Enemy gains +1 unless Rome commits at least two Legions.

scenarios.name: The Gathering Storm

mandate.name: Prepared Frontier
mandate.text: At the end, Lauriacum, Carnuntum, and Sirmium must each contain a Legion, be intact, and be free of enemy Armies.

scenarios.rule: The first Petition each game costs no Treasury.
scenarios.history: Pressure builds while disease and the eastern war limit Rome's freedom of action.

epilogue.victory: The frontier bends without breaking. Rome has bought the time needed to understand the scale of the northern war.
epilogue.defeat: The first warnings were answered too slowly. What seemed a frontier disturbance has become an imperial emergency.

scenarios.name: Italy Invaded

mandate.name: Road from Italy
mandate.text: At the end, Aquileia, Virunum, and Lauriacum must each be intact and free of enemy Armies.

scenarios.rule: The first time the Quadi Army enters Carnuntum, lose 1 additional Rome.
scenarios.history: A coalition breaks through the frontier and threatens Aquileia in northern Italy.

epilogue.victory: Aquileia endures. The invasion has been turned back, but Italy now understands that the Danube is no distant border.
epilogue.defeat: The road into Italy remains open. Confidence in the emperor and the frontier system collapses together.

scenarios.name: Beyond the Danube

mandate.name: Winter Camps
mandate.text: Establish winter camps by placing at least two Legions in Marcomannia at the same time.

scenarios.rule: Campaigns in Marcomannia gain +1 Roman total, but every Exertion there costs 1 Resolve.
scenarios.history: Marcus carries the war north, seeking leverage against the Marcomanni.

epilogue.victory: Roman camps stand beyond the river. The Marcomanni have learned that withdrawal does not end Marcus's purpose.
epilogue.defeat: The northern offensive spends men and endurance without securing the leverage Marcus sought.

scenarios.name: Among the Quadi

mandate.name: Rival Kings
mandate.text: In two different rounds, send Envoys while Quadi Strength is 3 or less; a Quadi settlement completes it.

scenarios.rule: Once per game after losing a battle, set both dice to 4; then lose 1 Treasury. This represents the contested rain-miracle tradition without choosing an explanation.
scenarios.history: The Quadi campaign combines hard fighting, disputed kingship, thirst, weather, and propaganda.

epilogue.victory: The Quadi submit to a settlement that force alone could not have made durable. Rome will remember the storm differently than those who stood beneath it.
epilogue.defeat: The campaign dissolves into exhaustion, disputed memory, and a peace too weak to outlast the season.

scenarios.name: The Sarmatian Plain

mandate.name: Terms on the Plain
mandate.text: Bring Iazyges Strength to 1 or less while holding Mercy 3 or more.

scenarios.rule: The Enemy die gains +1 on the Plain of the Iazyges unless at least three Legions are committed.
scenarios.history: Roman forces confront the mobile Iazyges and seek prisoners, auxiliaries, and a durable settlement.

epilogue.victory: The Iazyges yield prisoners and military service. Mobility has been answered by concentration, patience, and negotiated compulsion.
epilogue.defeat: The Sarmatian plain consumes Roman effort faster than decision can be forced.

scenarios.name: The Eastern Usurper

mandate.name: Legitimate Command
mandate.text: End two rounds at Senate 5 or more after using an Officium command.

scenarios.rule: Each Campaign costs 1 Treasury. The first time Senate reaches 5, gain 2 Momentum.
scenarios.history: Avidius Cassius is proclaimed emperor in the east, forcing Marcus to balance speed, legitimacy, and clemency.

epilogue.victory: The usurpation ends without turning clemency into weakness. Marcus returns north with legitimacy scarred but intact.
epilogue.defeat: The eastern revolt exposes a government unable to preserve both authority and restraint.

scenarios.name: The Second Expedition

mandate.name: Forward Occupation
mandate.text: End two rounds with Legions simultaneously in Marcomannia and the Lands of the Quadi.

scenarios.rule: At the end of rounds 4 and 7, lose 1 Resolve unless you Meditated that round.
scenarios.history: War resumes. Marcus pursues an unfinished northern settlement while age, fatigue, and succession narrow his time.

epilogue.victory: The second expedition leaves Rome near the settlement Marcus sought, though time rather than the enemy is now the greater power.
epilogue.defeat: The unfinished northern design passes into other hands. The frontier survives Marcus, but not in the form he intended.

scenarios.name: The Burden of the Danube

mandate.name: Three Burdens
mandate.text: After round 3 secure the Italian road; after round 6 hold Senate 4 and Mercy 2; make one treaty.

scenarios.rule: After rounds 3 and 6, reduce Fatigue and Coalition by 2, gain 1 Supply, and restore 1 to your lowest state track; then increase the highest Strength by 1. At round 8, lose 1 Resolve.
scenarios.history: A compressed full reign: epidemic, invasion, counteroffensive, revolt, renewed war, and the question of what peace will survive.

epilogue.victory: Marcus leaves no final victory, only a frontier made governable at terrible cost. Whether that settlement survives belongs to Commodus.
epilogue.defeat: The burdens of plague, invasion, revolt, and succession exceed the emperor's remaining strength. History receives an unfinished war.

commands.name: Redeploy the Vexillations
commands.imperium: March, then March again with one of the moved Legions.
commands.officium: Gain 1 Senate; then move one Legion one connection toward Aquileia.

commands.name: Secure the River
commands.imperium: Pay 1 Supply: reduce Strength by 1 for up to two Armies at or adjacent to bases containing Legions.

commands.name: Pompeianus Commands
commands.imperium: Campaign with +2 Roman total. Marcus cannot use Assent in that battle.
commands.officium: Gain 1 Senate and reduce Fatigue by 1.

commands.name: Raise New Legions
commands.imperium: Pay 3 Treasury: return one lost Legion to Aquileia.
commands.officium: Pay 2 Treasury and 1 Senate: return one lost Legion to Aquileia and gain 1 Rome.

commands.name: Fortify Italy and the Alps
commands.imperium: Reduce Raetian or Marcomanni Strength by 2; pay 1 Supply.

commands.name: Divide the Coalition
commands.imperium: Choose two Armies. Reduce one Strength by 2, increase the other by 1, and reduce Coalition by 1.
commands.officium: Spend 1 Senate: reduce any Army Strength by 1, gain 1 Mercy, and reduce Coalition by 2.

commands.name: Forced March
commands.imperium: Move up to three Legions through one extra connection; increase Fatigue by 1.

commands.name: Winter Quarters
commands.imperium: Reduce Fatigue by 2. You may Fortify once.
commands.officium: Gain 1 Resolve, 1 Supply, and 1 Senate; increase the highest Strength by 1.

commands.name: Address the Troops
commands.imperium: Campaign. On a tie or loss, gain 1 Resolve after consequences.
commands.officium: Gain 2 Resolve; lose 1 Senate unless Mercy is 3+.

commands.name: Take Hostages
commands.imperium: After winning a battle, reduce Army Strength by 1 more; lose 1 Mercy.
commands.officium: Gain 2 Senate if total Strength is 8 or less; otherwise gain 1 Treasury.

commands.name: Return the Prisoners
commands.imperium: Spend 1 Momentum: reduce an Army at Strength 2 or less to 0 and gain 2 Mercy.
commands.officium: Gain 1 Rome and 1 Mercy; lose 1 Treasury.

commands.name: Danube Fleet
commands.imperium: Move any number of Legions between Carnuntum and Sirmium, then gain +1 in a battle at Quadi or Iazyges.

commands.name: Council at Carnuntum
commands.imperium: Look at the next two Crises. Return them in either order, then Fortify.
commands.officium: Look at the next three Crises. Put one on the bottom.

commands.name: No More Than Duty
commands.imperium: Campaign without increasing Fatigue this round.
commands.officium: Meditate, then Petition without paying Treasury.

commands.name: Clemency After Victory
commands.imperium: Campaign. If you win, gain Mercy instead of Momentum and reduce Fatigue by 1.
commands.officium: Spend 1 Senate: gain 1 Mercy, 1 Rome, and 1 Resolve.

crises.name: Langobardi Cross the River
crises.design: If no Legion is at Carnuntum or with the Quadi Army, increase it by 1 again.

crises.name: Eleven Envoys
crises.arrival: Choose: spend 1 Senate to reduce the highest Strength by 1, or gain 1 Treasury and increase it by 1.
crises.design: Envoys conceal preparations on the western frontier.

crises.name: The Plague Returns
crises.arrival: Lose 1 Rome or remove one Legion to the lost box.

crises.name: Lucius Is Dead
crises.arrival: Lose 1 Resolve. Choose a space; Legions there cannot March this round.
crises.design: Gain 1 Senate if you used Officium.

crises.name: The Road to Aquileia
crises.arrival: Increase Marcomanni and Quadi Strength by 1.
crises.design: If their combined Strength is 8+, lose 1 Rome.

crises.name: Opitergium Burned
crises.arrival: Lose 1 Rome. Requisition gains 3 Supply this round.
crises.design: If you did not Campaign or Fortify, lose 1 Senate.

crises.name: Ballomar's Coalition
crises.design: Reduce a different Strength by 1 if you used diplomacy this round.

crises.name: The Costoboci Raid South
crises.arrival: Pay 2 Treasury or lose 1 Rome and 1 Senate.

crises.name: Across the Frozen Danube
crises.arrival: Campaigns against Quadi or Iazyges gain +1 this round; each Roman loss also costs 1 Supply.
crises.design: Increase Fatigue by 1 if you fought.

crises.name: The Rain and the Thirst
crises.design: If you used Assent, reduce the battled Army's Strength by 1.

crises.name: Ariogaesus Defies Rome
crises.arrival: Increase Quadi Strength by 2 unless you spend 1 Senate.
crises.design: If Quadi Strength is 1 or less, gain 1 Momentum.

crises.name: Horsemen of the Iazyges
crises.arrival: Move one Legion away from the Iazyges Army or increase its Strength by 2.
crises.design: The Enemy die gains +1 against Iazyges this round.

crises.name: One Hundred Thousand Captives
crises.arrival: Choose: gain 2 Rome, or gain 1 Mercy and reduce Iazyges Strength by 1.
crises.design: Lose 1 Supply if Iazyges is not pacified.

crises.name: Cassius Takes the Purple
crises.arrival: Lose 2 Senate. You may spend 2 Treasury to lose only 1.
crises.design: If Senate is 2 or less, lose 1 Rome.

crises.name: Commodus at the Front
crises.arrival: Gain 1 Rome or 1 Senate. Then lose 1 Resolve unless Mercy is 3+.
crises.design: If you Campaign, gain +1 Roman total and increase Fatigue by 1.

crises.name: Time Is a River
crises.arrival: Choose: lose 1 Resolve, or increase two Strengths by 1.
crises.design: If this is the final round, gain 1 VP for each pacified people.
